item.title: Catching cow burps in real time: Methane sensor matches industry monitor in early field test
item.description: Methane is a short-lived but powerful greenhouse gas; cutting methane emissions can slow near-term warming and improve air quality by reducing harmful ground-level ozone. As ruminants digest feed, they release methane—through burps. In fact, emissions from cattle are the largest source of human-caused methane emissions (roughly 25% of the total)—so reducing emissions from cattle is an important part of tackling climate change. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What happens inside a wildfire? A Ph.D. student is finding out
item.description: What happens during a wildfire? The short answer is: much more than we know. As wildfires burn through trees, grasses and other vegetation, heat from the flames sets off thousands of chemical reactions at once. Molecules break apart, recombine and transform into new compounds, releasing gases, soot and other carbon-rich particles into the air. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Dead fish have been removed from Poland's Gliwice Canal after a toxic algae bloom. This event mirrors the devastating 2022 ecological disaster in the Oder River system. Scientists warn climate change may increase the likelihood of such ecological crises. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: A forecast is not a decision: Design engineering for drought preparedness
item.description: More than 80 countries face chronic drought, yet only a third have systems in place to act before a drought arrives rather than after. The gap is costly. According to the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization, every $1 invested in anticipatory action can save up to $7 in averted losses, while also helping protect lives and livelihoods before crisis conditions take hold. Acting early works. So why don't more countries do it? Fuente: Phys.org.

Una de las más virales asegura, sin aportar pruebas, que el terremoto sería parte de un supuesto plan secreto acordado con Estados Unidos para reducir la población del país.
